text: AWS grew 39.3% year-over-year in Q3, its sixth straight quarter of acceleration and fastest growth in nearly five years, on a business now at a $184 billion annualized run rate.
AWS backlog reached $578 billion in Q3, growing triple digits year-over-year and well diversified, giving multi-year visibility into the reinvestment runway.
Management states AWS can grow north of 40% in each of 2027 and 2028 and become a $1 trillion revenue business within 5 to 10 years — a stated runway far longer than one year of pricing.

Absolute EBITDA has compounded from $15,584M (FY2017) to $183,719M (LTM Sep-30-2026) with EBITDA margin rising from 9% to 23%, so the trend is rising scale and rising profitability together — not a margin-funded illusion.

AWS operating margin was 38.7% in Q3 with operating income of $17.8 billion, and management says AI-side margins are improving well ahead of where core was at a similar stage — the heavy AI build is not yet eroding segment economics.

FY2025 segment operating income shows AWS earned $45,606M at a 35.4% margin versus North America $29,619M (6.9%) and International $4,750M (2.9%), so the highest-return segment is the one growing fastest.

Stores units grew nearly 15% year-to-date on a base of more than 30 billion items, adding more than $90 billion of gross sales in the trailing 12 months — about double the gross sales per quarter of the next largest US competitor.
Revenue consensus rises steadily to FY2027E $949,994M, implying the long-duration growth the price embeds is corroborated by sell-side forecasts across multiple fiscal years.
Interest coverage is 41x and net-debt/EBITDA is 1.0x, so the company can fund an enormous reinvestment program without balance-sheet strain.

On comps the name carries EBITDA growth of 33% vs peer-median 20% and LT EPS growth 23% vs peer-median 13% at a similar 23% EBITDA margin, so its discount to the LTM peer median (EV/EBITDA 13.8x vs 14.6x) is paired with materially better growth, posing whether that discount is EARNED or RESIDUAL — a question for the human, not a computed upside; the peer set is flagged HETEROGENEOUS so read it as a confidence-gated input.

LTM levered free cash flow is -$34,731.8M and the FCF sign is negative, so despite rising EBITDA the company is burning cash — the self-fund read is MIXED (latest-Q OCF positive, LTM FCF negative, and both must be positive to self-fund).

2026 cash CapEx is guided to approximately $220 billion with management expecting to spend meaningfully more in 2027, the cause behind the FCF deficit and the reason returns depend on data centers being monetized years out.

The trailing P/E of 34.3x is not an operating anchor: three of the last four quarters carry a material below-the-line block netting +$78,919M, including a Gain (Loss) On Sale Of Invest. of $69,158.0M in the LTM — the GAAP EPS and trailing P/E both inflate on non-operating items, so the optical multiple is a MISREAD, not the real earnings signal.

EV/EBITDA (TEV/LTM) at 15.1x sits at the 3rd percentile of its own 9.2-year range (14.2–49.0x, median 24.4x), but this is trailing-only with no forward basis — the near-floor reading cannot by itself distinguish a temporarily depressed level from a structurally lower terminal one.

North America segment revenue growth decelerated to 6% year-over-year in Q3 (from 16% in Q2), and even adjusted for the Prime Day timing shift of ~400bps the core retail top line is slowing against a very large base.

Forward EV/EBITDA and adjusted EPS cannot be read at the drawdown because no revised guidance was available, so the overshoot-vs-terminal question on the near-floor trailing 15.1x multiple is unresolved (neither bull nor bear).

The 5-year P/E percentile cannot be built because a stock split inside the window divides split-adjusted prices against as-filed older EPS (~20.01x basis mismatch); the current 34.3x P/E stands but has no historical context.

Segment EBITDA is not disclosed — only segment operating income is reported — so AWS's standalone cash economics and incremental margin on the AI build cannot be isolated from the consolidated figure; this missing breakout is a bearish opacity, not a neutral gap.

The covenant leverage basis and company-adjusted LTM EBITDA are UNKNOWN (not disclosed), so no covenant-basis leverage read is possible; the maturity wall on the 10-Q basis is NOT_STATED (no near-term maturity), a known rather than unknown.

CIQ's EBITDA is a vendor-normalised figure: its LTM ($181,219M) differs from the filing LTM ($183,719M) and the quarter to 2025-12-31 differs by -$2,500M, so every EV/EBITDA on the page divides a normalised denominator — read trailing-vs-forward multiples across the actual/estimate boundary as part definitional.
The consensus-basis FCF stays negative (FY26E -$34,360M, FY27E -$18,090M), so the timing of any crossover to positive free cash flow from the capex cycle is unresolved.
Insider activity shows 63 open-market sells by 8 insiders ($411.65M) over 182 days and zero buys over the 3-year scan — a signal the human must weigh.
Short interest is rising (+8.1% to 93.7M shares at the latest settle), though still only ~0.9% of shares outstanding.

text: mixed — rising absolute EBITDA and double-digit constant-currency growth offset by a GAAP earnings collapse, negative FCF and high post-acquisition leverage.

The decline is idiosyncratic and driven by a cited, identifiable set of transitory pressures (inventory charge, freight, price/mix) rather than a demand collapse — the RTD shake category itself grew ~8% in Q2, well ahead of the broader food/beverage industry.

Absolute EBITDA has compounded strongly through FY25 ($117M FY17 → $445M FY25) even as the LTM figure fell to $332M, so the business franchise that generated the cash is intact and the recent drop is from an elevated base, not a structural zero.

Management has already enacted a mechanism to restore margin: a double-digit Premier shake price increase plus powder pricing effective Q1 FY27, which they frame as necessary to offset input inflation and rebuild the margin profile.

Underlying demand metrics remain healthy — Premier household penetration has reached almost 23% with the highest shake repeat rate in the category — supporting the overshoot-vs-terminal reading on volume.
The business is self-funding and solvent: LTM levered FCF of $201.1M and FCF-positive sign support the overshoot case against a terminal read.
Capital allocation signals conviction: a $600M buyback was authorized Nov-2025 and the share count fell ~9.7% over ~1.7 years, shrinking the base that the recovering earnings accrue to.

On a forward basis the de-rating looks less extreme than the trailing P/E of 6.3x suggests — P/FY27E normalized is ~7.2x and P/FY26E normalized ~9.2x, so the headline trailing multiple overstates cheapness only if forward earnings recover as consensus models.
Q3 FY26 net sales grew 4% with both brands ahead of plan, indicating the top line was stabilizing into the latest print rather than deteriorating further.

The EBITDA margin fall is partly REAL signal, not just optics: LTM EBITDA margin dropped to 14% from 19-21% while absolute LTM EBITDA also FELL to $332M from $445M FY25 — here the % decline is corroborated by an absolute decline, so this is a genuine profit contraction, not a denominator illusion.

The gross-margin collapse is mechanism-backed and severe: adjusted gross margin fell to 22.7% from 34.5% a year earlier on input-cost inflation, tariffs, unfavorable price/mix and freight — a structural cost problem, not a one-quarter blip.

Competitive intensity is pressuring the core: 27% of RTD shake category volume sold on promotion in Q2 (up 8 pts YoY) and 70% in Q3, with the first decline in RTD buy rate in 5 years — the moat may be eroding as insurgent brands invest aggressively.

Consensus has violently cut forward estimates: FY26 EBITDA consensus fell ~43% (505.3 → 288.1) and FY26 normalized EPS ~56% over 12 months, so the trailing multiple is dividing a price into earnings that are themselves still being revised down.

Leverage is elevated versus the group — net-debt/EBITDA 3.4x and total-debt/EBITDA 3.5x vs peer median 2.4x — so a prolonged earnings depression carries real balance-sheet strain, with interest coverage only 4.2x.

Leadership is in transition at the worst moment: the CEO/President retired and a new CEO started with seven days' tenure at the Q3 call, and the Chief Growth Officer departed — execution risk is heightened precisely when a turnaround must be delivered.

The announced FY27 price increase carries elasticity risk management itself flags as slightly greater than 1, meaning volume could fall more than price rises — the margin-repair lever may not translate cleanly to EBITDA.

The stock's decline is overwhelmingly idiosyncratic: BRBR fell ~41.6% over 180d while the small-cap benchmark was roughly flat (-1.9%), a ~-39.6% relative move signalling a name-specific re-rating rather than a market swoon.

No forward adjusted EBITDA or adjusted EPS in the revised FY26 guidance — the adjusted-basis forward earnings power is undisclosed, an opacity risk given the EBITDA-basis estimate/actual check is UNRESOLVED (GAAP actuals vs possibly adjusted estimates in the 1.5-2.0x band).
Whether the announced FY27 double-digit price increase holds net of >1 elasticity and competitive promotion — the actual volume response is unknown until the next prints.

CIQ's EBITDA is vendor-normalised and runs $69M above the filing-rebuilt LTM figure ($401M vs $332M) due to a legal-settlement add-back; which EBITDA each multiple divides must be confirmed before trusting any leverage or EV/EBITDA read.
Peer set is HETEROGENEOUS (market caps $228M–$33.9B, 149x span); the peer median is not a clean benchmark and every peer-relative stat is confidence-gated.

No forward basis for the 6.4x EV/EBITDA (trailing only) — cannot distinguish a temporarily depressed level from a permanently impaired one; this near-floor multiple is a neutral fact, not directional.
New CEO's strategic priorities and FY27 guidance are not yet disclosed (promised for the Q4 call) — the turnaround plan's substance is unknown.
Single-segment reporting (Protein-Based Consumer Goods) means no brand-level or Premier-vs-Dymatize EBITDA split to isolate where the margin damage sits.
Whether protein-driven commodity inflation that management says worsens into Q4 continues into FY27, and at what level, is unquantified.

text: mixed — genuine transitory/turnaround levers (pricing, category growth, self-funding) are offset by a real, mechanism-backed margin collapse, elevated leverage and leadership transition.

The drawdown is idiosyncratic and sharp — the name fell 24% over 180 days while the mid-cap benchmark was roughly flat, as a gradual bleed with no discrete gap-down, so the de-rate is a sentiment unwind rather than a disclosed impairment.

The EV/EBITDA multiple sits at its own-history near-floor (8%ile of 38 quarterly closes, 9.0x vs median 12.8x) even as the underlying business is compounding, framing the move as an overshoot off trough sentiment rather than a terminal re-rating.

Absolute EBITDA is rising steadily through the de-rate — $1,048M (FY25) → $1,241M (FY26) → $1,361M LTM — so the lower multiple is being applied to a larger, growing earnings base, not a shrinking one.

Operating margin EXPANDED 100bps in Q2, well above the guided 60bps, a high-quality beat driven by merchandise margin plus supply-chain and SG&A leverage on only 2% comp — the earnings engine is intact, not impaired.

New-store expansion is the structural growth driver — 178 gross / 149 net new stores on a trailing-12-month basis — and management raised full-year guidance, pointing to revenue momentum that is self-generated rather than cyclical.
Sales productivity has stepped up structurally (around $350/sq ft vs ~$220 in 2019, a 55% gain) as growth shifts into smaller, more productive formats, supporting future occupancy leverage.
The business is self-funding with ample coverage — FCF-positive, interest coverage 18.4x, and ~$1.6B total liquidity with an undrawn ABL — so survival is not in question even at 3.8x net-debt/EBITDA.

On growth metrics the name screens AHEAD of the peer median — revenue growth 11% vs 9%, EBITDA growth 22% vs 13%, LT EPS growth 17% vs 8% — posing whether any valuation premium is EARNED by superior fundamentals rather than a value trap; note the peer set is heterogeneous ($2.8B–$143.1B caps) so this is a confidence-gated read.
Sell-side remains constructive post-drawdown with a Buy consensus and mean target $364.75 vs a $247.63 close, indicating analysts read the move as dislocation rather than deterioration.

A genuine counter-point, OUTWEIGHED by rising absolute EBITDA and 100bps margin expansion: the headline cross-sectional multiples sit at a PREMIUM to peers (EV/EBITDA 9.0x vs 7.1x median, +27%; P/E 22.9x vs 16.3x, +40%), but the peer set is HETEROGENEOUS ($2.8B–$143.1B, 51x cap spread) so the 'premium' is a confidence-gated optical read, not a clean terminal signal.

A genuine counter-point, OUTWEIGHED by 18.4x interest coverage and self-funding FCF: leverage runs richer than peers at 2.5x total-debt/EBITDA (3.8x net-debt) vs peer median 1.6x, and the S&P issuer rating is BB+ (sub-investment-grade) — a real structural gap but not a near-term solvency threat.

A genuine counter-point, OUTWEIGHED by raised FY guidance and 100bps margin beat: forward estimate revisions skewed DOWNWARD into the drawdown — Guggenheim cut FY27 EPS normalized to $11.17 and the next-2-quarter breadth is heavily negative (EBITDA FQ3/FQ4 0 up / 8 down) — signalling near-term consensus softening even as the full-year guide rose.

A genuine counter-point, OUTWEIGHED by management's stated economics of the program: underlying comp growth is decelerating to 2% in Q2 (from 6% in Q1), partly because new-store cannibalization is now worth ~1.5pts of comp — the growth is increasingly expansion-driven rather than same-store demand.

A genuine counter-point, OUTWEIGHED by FCF-positive self-funding: capex has ballooned ($493M FY24 → $880M FY25 → $1,060M FY26) driving FCF down to a thin $105–107M LTM despite strong CFO, so the aggressive store rollout is consuming most of the cash it generates.

A genuine counter-point, OUTWEIGHED by consistent recent delivery (EPS floor beaten 49/52): insiders sold $14.3M across 47 open-market sales with zero buys over 182 days, offering no insider conviction at the depressed price.

No forward/adjusted EV/EBITDA basis is available at the drawdown (ev_ebitda_adjusted_fwd UNKNOWN), so the trailing 9.0x cannot be cleanly distinguished from a forward-depressed level — the overshoot-vs-terminal question stays open.

Single-segment reporting (Retail-Apparel) with no segment-EBITDA breakout and no disclosed customers — the opacity means the consolidated number cannot be decomposed to isolate where comp softness is concentrated (treat as a bearish disclosure gap).
The $297.1M 1.25% convertible matures 2027-12-15; wall coherence is UNKNOWN from the filing and no refinance/repay path is disclosed — a near-term capital-structure item left unresolved.
Covenant basis for the 3.8x leverage is UNKNOWN (not disclosed); the springing fixed-charge covenant exists but headroom at the depressed price is not quantifiable from the facts.

Whether the tariff-refund reinvestment into 'sharper values' in the back half protects comp or masks underlying demand softness — management frames it as neutral to full-year earnings but the comp effect is not isolable.
The actual trigger for the 24% idiosyncratic bleed is not identified (no catalyst 8-K, no gap-down) — the market's specific concern is unstated and must be resolved independently.

text: strongly-bullish — multiple at own-history floor while absolute EBITDA, margins and guidance all rise on a self-funding, growing base.

The GAAP loss is driven by non-cash goodwill impairment, not operating collapse: FY26 consensus crossed to -$852M GAAP net income after a $1,050M goodwill impairment, while adjusted EPS guidance holds at $10.97–$11.09 — the P/E 'NM' is the impairment, not an earnings disappearance.

The trailing EV/EBITDA 4.1x is struck on CIQ's own normalised EBITDA (TEV with leases over EBITDA with rent), NOT on the filing's GAAP number which the $1,050M+ unusual items drag to LTM $-1,436M — so the headline multiple measures the operating business, not the impaired GAAP one.

The business is self-funding with FCF-positive capacity: LTM levered FCF $806M and OCF $787M positive, supporting the stated $550M+ gross-debt paydown and net leverage reduction toward ~2.6x at year-end.

The AI/transformation pivot is reaching scale: management states 50% of revenue now comes from businesses built in the last 3 years, growing ~30% YoY, more profitable and 4x stickier, expected to exceed $6B in 2027.

Client base is deep and retained — 98% retention, >16-year tenure with top-25 clients, and all top-5 plus >90% of top-100 clients have expanded into new services since FY2023 — arguing against terminal client flight.

On the forward lens the name screens far below a HETEROGENEOUS peer set (NTM TEV/EBITDA name 4.8 vs peer median 8.45; NTM P/E 2.87 vs 11.23) — but with the peer gap partly EARNED by weaker fundamentals (margin 12% vs 18%, rev growth 3% vs 8%, LT EPS growth 5% vs 10%), the human must judge whether the residual beyond those deltas is overshoot.

The $1,050M goodwill impairment is a real signal of overpayment: it follows a $1,523M FY25 write-down, so $2,573M of goodwill has been impaired against ~$1,914M paid for the FY23 Webhelp-era acquisition — a genuine load-bearing marker of destroyed acquisition value, not a pure non-cash cosmetic.

Returns on capital have structurally de-rated and not recovered: ROIC fell from 9.0% (FY22) to 3.8% (FY24) and sits at just 4.4% LTM — the business earns a low return on a leveraged capital base, a real quality signal beneath the cheap multiple.
